title: The Slow Songbook
premise: Gideon Eriksen, a celebrated ghostwriter who hides behind other people's words, is hired anonymously to write the memoirs of Vivienne Ashford—a rival biographer who once publicly humiliated him and who is quietly losing her memory to early-onset dementia. Neither knows who is on the other end of the assignment's encrypted portal, and through exchanged voice notes and manuscript pages they begin a correspondence that softens into something neither will name. When Gideon discovers the memoir he is writing is the only record Vivienne will have of her own life—and that she has been concealing how fast she is deteriorating—he must choose between finishing invisibly, as he always has, or revealing himself and risking her fury with the little time she has left to forgive him. In the end, he steps out of the shadows at her final public reading; she recognizes his cadence before his face, and together they finish the last chapter in her own hand, turning a ghostwritten life into an inheritance she gives willingly.
about_author: Coral Okafor is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing other people's letters before turning to fiction, and her novels are known for their tenderness toward the unfinished sentence. She lives in Lisbon with her partner and a growing collection of unposted postcards.

chapters.title: The Ghost's Contract
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He accepts a lucrative anonymous memoir assignment through a literary agency's encrypted portal, relieved to work without a face or a name. A flashback establishes the humiliation Vivienne Ashford dealt him at a literary festival years ago. Emotional beat: the comfort and cost of invisibility.

chapters.title: Voice Without a Face
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. She begins recording voice notes for her anonymous ghostwriter, sharp, funny, and withholding, dictating from a house that feels too large. A small forgotten word alarms her more than she admits. Emotional beat: pride masking fear.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The correspondence begins; her voice is maddeningly familiar, and he finds himself arguing with her in his drafts. He sets strict rules for the assignment—no identities, no past. Emotional beat: the first crack in professional detachment.

chapters.title: What the House Remembers
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. She walks her childhood home for a chapter on inheritance, describing her mother's songbook and a melody she can no longer fully recall. The ghostwriter's gentle follow-up questions unsettle her. Emotional beat: memory as both wound and inheritance.

chapters.title: Cadence
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He recognizes her mother's songbook from an article he once admired—and realizes he knows her work intimately, better than she knows his. He almost signs a reply with his real name, then doesn't. Emotional beat: temptation toward honesty.

chapters.title: The Missing Hour
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. She loses an hour in a supermarket car park and lies to her sister about it, then lies to the ghostwriter by omission, skipping the incident from her dictation. Emotional beat: the first deliberate concealment.

chapters.title: Drafts and Counterdrafts
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Their editorial sparring turns playful, almost flirtatious; he catches himself writing sentences to make her laugh. He researches her publicly and finds the festival clip of their old clash, guilt sharpening. Emotional beat: affection arriving under false pretenses.

chapters.title: The Sister's Suspicions
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. Her sister Nell finds a neurologist's brochure and confronts her; Vivienne deflects, then secretly books an appointment alone. She dictates a chapter about her mother's loyalty to a man who never claimed her. Emotional beat: inherited patterns of hiding.

chapters.title: Diagnosis in the Margins
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He notices gaps in her timeline—repeated anecdotes, a forgotten name—and, as a professional, knows what they mean. He asks one careful question; she goes silent for four days. Emotional beat: dread disguised as editorial concern.

chapters.title: Confession, Partially
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. She admits to the ghostwriter that she is 'unwell,' without naming it, and asks him to promise the book will be finished no matter what. Gideon, reading, makes the promise aloud to an empty room. Emotional beat: a vow made to a stranger who isn't one.

chapters.title: The Songbook's Last Page
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. She finds her mother's unfinished final song and dictates the story of it, weeping mid-recording, then asks the ghostwriter—almost tenderly—to tell her something true about himself. Emotional beat: intimacy outpacing anonymity.

chapters.title: Something True
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He gives her a true story—about his father, about why he writes other people's lives—edited just enough to stay unrecognizable. She replies that she wishes she'd known him in another life. Emotional beat: love declared in the conditional tense.

chapters.title: The Festival Invitation
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. She is invited to give a farewell reading and accepts impulsively, telling Nell it's for the book's publicity. Privately she wants one night where she is still entirely herself. Emotional beat: defiance against disappearing.

chapters.title: Two Tickets
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. His agent reveals the memoir will be published under Vivienne's name with a live launch—her farewell reading. He realizes he could attend and see her face for the first time in years. Emotional beat: the pull between safety and witness.

chapters.title: What Nell Found
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. Nell discovers the neurology reports and the anonymous correspondence, and accuses Vivienne of handing her life to a stranger while pushing away everyone who loves her. Vivienne, frightened, freezes the portal. Emotional beat: loyalty weaponized into isolation.

chapters.title: Silence on the Line
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Cut off mid-book, he rereads every transcript and finally understands the shape of what's happening—and how little time she has. He decides to finish the manuscript and deliver it in person, whatever it costs. Emotional beat: resolve born of love.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. At the farewell reading, Vivienne falters mid-passage; from the back row, Gideon continues the sentence from memory—his own sentence, from her own book. She knows the cadence instantly. Emotional beat: exposure as devotion.

chapters.title: You
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. Backstage, fury and recognition collide; she throws the old humiliation at him, then breaks, asking why he never said. He answers with the truth about the assignment and the diagnosis he pieced together. Emotional beat: rage giving way to grief.

chapters.title: The Last Chapter
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. They write the final chapter together at her kitchen table, her hand on the page, his voice steadying hers, the songbook open between them. She dictates an ending she chooses rather than one that happens to her. Emotional beat: authorship reclaimed.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The memoir publishes with a co-credit buried in the acknowledgments—her insistence. He turns down the next ghostwriting contract and begins, badly and gladly, to write under his own name. Emotional beat: stepping out of the past tense.

chapters.title: The Slow Song
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. On a good morning, she plays her mother's songbook while Gideon finishes the melody she once lost; on a bad one, he keeps the thread for her. She begins recording a new voice journal—not a memoir, but letters forward. Emotional beat: tenderness inside loss.

chapters.title: Coda: In the First Person
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs, epilogue. At the book's launch a year later, Vivienne introduces Gideon by name to a room that once watched her shame him. He reads the final page aloud; she corrects one word, and it is better. Emotional beat: a whole heart, risked and kept.
